Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction under a Two-fold Fay-Herriot Model.

Source: R/eblup_twofold.R
eblup_twofold.Rd

This function gives the Empirical Best Linear Unbiased Prediction (EBLUP) under a two-fold Fay-Herriot model (Torabi & Rao, 2014): subareas nested within areas with an area random effect \(v_i\) and a subarea random effect \(u_{ij}\).

Usage

eblup_twofold(
  formula,
  vardir,
  domain = NULL,
  subarea = NULL,
  data,
  method = c("REML", "ML"),
  mse_type = c("analytical", "bootstrap", "none"),
  B = 100,
  seed = -1,
  maxiter = 100,
  precision = 1e-04,
  self_benchmark = FALSE,
  benchmark_weight = NULL,
  benchmark_target = NULL,
  benchmark_group = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  compute_area = TRUE,
  print_result = TRUE
)

Arguments

formula

an object of class formula that contains a description of the model to be fitted.

vardir

sampling variances of the sub-area direct estimates: a numeric vector, the name of a column of data or a one-sided formula.

domain

vector, column name or one-sided formula referencing the area identifier column in data. Must be supplied.

subarea

vector, column name or one-sided formula referencing the subarea identifier column in data. If NULL, rows are numbered consecutively.

data

a data frame or a data frame extension (e.g. a tibble), one row per subarea.

method

Fitting method can be chosen between 'REML' and 'ML'.

mse_type

MSE estimator: 'analytical' (default; Prasad-Rao g1+g2+2*g3, fast; ML adds the bias correction), 'bootstrap' (parametric bootstrap, slower but robust) or 'none' (no MSE; mse and rse are NA).

B

number of parametric bootstrap replicates (only used if mse_type = 'bootstrap').

seed

integer seed for the bootstrap; -1 (default) or NULL sets no seed. A fixed seed does not change the random number stream of the session.

maxiter

maximum number of iterations allowed in the Fisher-scoring algorithm.

precision

convergence tolerance limit for the Fisher-scoring algorithm.

self_benchmark

Logical. If TRUE, fits a self-benchmarking model via the augmented model approach (Wang, Fuller, and Qu, 2008; Rao and Molina, 2015, Sec 10.5.1), ensuring that the weighted aggregate of small area estimates automatically matches the direct survey aggregate or specified benchmark targets without post-hoc adjustment.

benchmark_weight

Optional vector, column name, or one-sided formula referencing the domain benchmarking weights in data (e.g. population sizes or shares). Defaults to equal weights.

benchmark_target

Optional numeric scalar or named vector specifying fixed aggregate benchmark target(s). If NULL (default), calibrates to the weighted aggregate of the direct estimates.

benchmark_group

Optional vector, column name, or one-sided formula referencing the grouping / stratum column in data (e.g. area identifier for subarea-to-area benchmarking) for group-specific self-benchmarking.

weight

Optional vector, column name or one-sided formula referencing the sub-area weights \(w_{ij}\) (e.g. population sizes) used for the area means \(\theta_i = \sum_j w_{ij}\theta_{ij}\). They are normalised within each area; if NULL, every sub-area of an area gets the same weight. Missing or negative weights get weight 0 (with a warning), as in hb_twofold.

compute_area

Logical. If TRUE (default), adds the EBLUPs of the area means and their MSE in df_area (see Details).

print_result

print coefficient or not, default value is TRUE.

Value

The function returns a list with the following objects: estcoef a data frame with the estimated model coefficients (beta), their standard errors (std.error, repeated as stderr_beta for compatibility with fastsae 0.1.0), z-statistics (zvalue) and normal p-values (pvalue), random_effect_var named vector with the estimated area (sigma2_v) and subarea (sigma2_u) variances (paper notation), goodness named vector: loglikelihood (the full Gaussian log-likelihood at the estimates, for ML and REML fits alike), AIC and BIC computed from it, following the convention of sae for the Fay-Herriot models; BIC uses the number of sampled subareas. The restricted (REML) likelihood is not reported: it depends on the covariates through X, so it cannot compare models with different covariates., df_eblup a data frame that contains domain, subarea, y, eblup, vardir, random_effect_area, random_effect_subarea, mse, and rse.
df_area (if compute_area = TRUE) a data frame with one row per area: domain, eblup_area, mse_area, rse_area, n_subareas (sub-areas in data) and n_sampled (those with a direct estimate).

Details

The model has a form that is response ~ auxiliary variables, with one row per subarea. When the response contains NA the subarea is treated as non-sampled. It is predicted by \(x_{ij}'\hat\beta + \hat v_i\), borrowing the area effect from the sampled sub-areas of its area; only the sub-areas of an area without any sampled sub-area get the synthetic estimator \(x_{ij}'\hat\beta\). MSE is estimated either analytically (Prasad-Rao g1+g2+2*g3 for REML, minus the ML bias term b'grad(g1) for ML, with an exact matrix derivation for g3) or by parametric bootstrap.

Area means. The target of area \(i\) is \(\theta_i = \sum_j w_{ij}\theta_{ij}\) over the sub-areas of the area in data (sampled or not), with the normalised weight. Its EBLUP is \(\sum_j w_{ij}\tilde\theta_{ij}\). The analytical MSE is the same second-order estimator as for the sub-areas, applied to this linear target (Torabi and Rao, 2014, derive it for population-weighted area means): it includes the covariance of the sub-area prediction errors through the shared area effect and \(\hat\beta\), so it is not \(\sum_j w_{ij}^2\,\mathrm{mse}_{ij}\). An area without sampled sub-areas gets the synthetic estimator \(\bar x_i'\hat\beta\) with MSE \(\bar x_i' Q \bar x_i + \hat\sigma_v^2 + \hat\sigma_u^2\sum_j w_{ij}^2\). With mse_type = "bootstrap" the area MSE comes from the same bootstrap replicates. Sub-areas of the population that are not rows of data are not part of the area mean.

References

  1. Torabi, M., & Rao, J. N. K. (2014). On small area estimation under a sub-area level model. Journal of Multivariate Analysis, 127, 36–55.

  2. Rao, J. N. K., & Molina, I. (2015). Small Area Estimation. John Wiley & Sons.

See also

hb_twofold for the hierarchical Bayes counterpart, and vignette("twofold-subarea", package = "fastsae").

Examples

library(fastsae)

# Two-fold Fay-Herriot model (simulated illustration)
set.seed(1)
m <- 20
dat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:m, function(d) {
  nd <- sample(2:5, 1)
  data.frame(
    area = d, subarea = paste0(d, "-", seq_len(nd)),
    x1 = rnorm(nd), y = NA_real_, vardir = runif(nd, 0.2, 1)
  )
}))
dat$y <- 1 + dat$x1 + rnorm(m)[dat$area] + rnorm(nrow(dat), sd = 0.5) +
  rnorm(nrow(dat), sd = sqrt(dat$vardir))
m1 <- eblup_twofold(y ~ x1,
  vardir = "vardir", domain = "area",
  subarea = "subarea", data = dat
)
